newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said on Friday.

"Government securities were narrowly today amid uncertainty over the near term direction of the market. Treasury bills yields were slightly lower but bond prices were slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.55/1.50 percent compared with Thursday's yield of 1.60/1.55 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.61/1.56 percent against 1.70/1.65 percent.
Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$99.55/99.60 from Thursday's close of S$99.50/99.55, September 2001 at S$96.83/96.88 versus S$96.72/96.77 and June 2003 at S$94.83/94.88 against S$94.72/94.77.
The interbank rate was unchanged from Thursday's 3-1/2 3-3/8 percent.
